questions.stem: A cell exposed to a drug that destroys spindle fibers arrests in mitosis instead of completing division. Which checkpoint failed to be satisfied, and what does the arrest protect against?
options: The spindle assembly checkpoint; it prevents a cell from separating chromosomes that are not attached to both poles
The G1 restriction point; it prevents replication of DNA that has not been repaired
The G2 checkpoint; it prevents entry into mitosis with incompletely condensed chromosomes
There is no metaphase checkpoint, so the arrest reflects nonspecific drug toxicity
questions.why: The spindle assembly checkpoint holds the cell at metaphase until every kinetochore is attached to opposite poles; otherwise chromosomes segregate unequally.

questions.stem: "Later start times do raise busing costs, and that cost is real. It is also smaller than the cost of the remediation a sleep-deprived student body requires." The writer's main purpose in the first sentence is to
options: establish a neutral, objective tone before the argument begins
refute the opposing view by dismissing it as unimportant
grant an opponent's point in order to sharpen the contrast with a larger countervailing cost
shift the burden of proof onto the reader
questions.why: The concession acknowledges a genuine cost, then subordinates it to a larger one, which makes the rebuttal look measured rather than defensive.

questions.stem: In E. coli, the lac operon is transcribed at high levels only when lactose is present and glucose is scarce. Which pair of conditions best explains why both signals are required?
options: Lactose binds the repressor and glucose binds the operator, so both must act on DNA directly
Lactose activates the repressor and glucose removes it, so the two signals are redundant
Glucose binds CAP and lactose binds RNA polymerase, and transcription needs both contacts
Lactose removes the repressor from the operator, while low glucose raises cAMP so CAP activates transcription
questions.why: Expression requires relief of repression plus activation: allolactose inactivates the repressor, and cAMP-CAP binds upstream to recruit RNA polymerase.

questions.stem: A school-board essay opens with a pediatrician's ten-year record of adolescent sleep studies, then closes with one parent's account of a 5 a.m. bus ride. The pairing mainly
options: substitutes an emotional appeal for evidence the board would find credible
couples expert credibility with a concrete human stake, so the data and the person reinforce each other
undercuts the pediatrician's authority by introducing an unrelated anecdote
signals that the writer has no statistical evidence and is shifting to narrative
questions.why: The appeals cooperate: the physician supplies ethos and logos, the parent supplies pathos anchored in one specific case.

questions.stem: After a first exposure to a pathogen a person becomes ill; on a second exposure to the same pathogen years later the person is briefly ill or asymptomatic. Which change in the immune system best explains the difference?
options: Innate barriers thicken after exposure and block entry of the pathogen the second time
The pathogen is destroyed by complement proteins that were absent during the first exposure
Memory B and T cells from the first exposure expand rapidly and produce antibody before symptoms develop
The second exposure is too small a dose to trigger any immune response at all
questions.why: Adaptive immunity is clonal and specific: memory lymphocytes persist, so the secondary response is faster and larger than the primary one.

questions.stem: "The policy failed because it was announced without notice, because it was funded without a plan, and because no one was consulted." The writer should revise the third element mainly to
options: shorten the sentence by removing the repetition of "because"
add a fourth element so the list feels complete
replace the first two elements with a single summary clause
restore parallel structure: "and because it was adopted without consultation"
questions.why: The first two items follow the same "because it was + verb phrase" pattern; restoring it to the third is what makes the triad land.

questions.stem: On the lagging strand during DNA replication, synthesis occurs in short Okazaki fragments rather than one continuous stretch. Which best explains that pattern?
options: The lagging strand template is chemically different, so polymerase cannot read it continuously
DNA polymerase can only extend from a free 3' end, and the lagging template runs the other way, so synthesis must restart repeatedly
The lagging strand lacks a primer, so replication there depends entirely on repair enzymes
Helicase opens the lagging strand more slowly, producing gaps that are later sealed
questions.why: Polymerase extends only 5' to 3', which forces discontinuous synthesis on the template oriented away from the fork; ligase later joins the fragments.

questions.stem: "The district installed a $40,000 scoreboard to celebrate academic achievement, and the ceremony ran long enough that students missed fourth period." The sentence works mainly through
options: situational irony: a celebration of academics costs students class time
hyperbole: the cost of the scoreboard is exaggerated for effect
verbal irony: the writer says the opposite of what is meant about the ceremony
personification: the scoreboard is credited with academic achievement
questions.why: The outcome undercuts the stated purpose, which is situational irony; nothing in the sentence is exaggerated or said in reverse.

questions.stem: A grassland supports grasses, grasshoppers, and hawks. If 10,000 units of energy enter the grasses, roughly how much reaches the hawks, and why?
options: About 5,000 units, because half the energy moves up at each transfer
About 10,000 units, because energy is conserved as it moves through a food chain
About 1,000 units, because most energy is lost in respiration at each transfer and there are only two transfers
About 100 units, because roughly 10 percent is retained per transfer and the hawks sit two transfers above the grasses
questions.why: Trophic efficiency is about 10 percent per level: 10,000 to about 1,000 in grasshoppers to about 100 in hawks, the rest lost mainly as heat.

questions.stem: "This program will eliminate the achievement gap." Which revision is most likely to strengthen the claim for a skeptical faculty audience?
options: "This program is guaranteed to eliminate the achievement gap completely."
"This program might possibly help somewhat with parts of the achievement gap."
"This program should narrow the gap in ninth-grade reading within two years, based on the three district pilots."
"This program will eliminate the achievement gap, as any reasonable person can see."
questions.why: A bounded, time-limited claim tied to cited evidence is more credible than an absolute promise or a content-free hedge.

questions.stem: A population of fish varies in body size. Anglers keep only the largest fish, while smaller fish slip through the nets. Which pattern of selection does this impose on body size, and with what expected effect?
options: Directional selection toward smaller body size: large individuals are removed before reproducing, shifting the mean down over generations
Stabilizing selection: mid-sized fish are favored and both extremes are removed
Disruptive selection: both large and small fish are favored over mid-sized fish
No selection, because fishing is not a natural environmental pressure
questions.why: Removing one extreme shifts the population mean generation after generation, which is the signature of directional selection.

questions.stem: A student writes: "Later start times improve attendance (Chen 14). Students arrive more rested and miss fewer first periods." Which revision best integrates the source?
options: Later start times improve attendance (Chen 14) (Chen 14). Students arrive more rested and miss fewer first periods.
Chen's district study found attendance gains of four percent after start times moved later, and she attributes them to students arriving more rested (14).
Later start times improve attendance. Students arrive more rested. Miss fewer first periods. (Chen)
As everyone knows, later start times improve attendance, and Chen agrees (14).
questions.why: Integrated citation names the source and its finding, so the evidence is part of the sentence rather than a dropped parenthetical.

questions.stem: A mutation changes a codon, but the resulting protein is unchanged. Which feature of the genetic code best explains this?
options: The code is overlapping, so a changed base is read twice and the effect cancels out
The code is universal, so the same codon is read identically in every organism
The code is redundant: several codons specify the same amino acid, so a changed third base can still place the same residue
The code is read in the cytoplasm, where free nucleotides correct errors before translation
questions.why: Degeneracy means multiple codons map to one amino acid, so a silent substitution leaves the polypeptide identical.

questions.stem: An essay about a school closure describes the gym floor: the taped line from a graduation rehearsal, the folded bleachers, the smell of floor wax. The writer most likely chooses these details to
options: make the loss concrete by preserving ordinary traces of the life the building held
establish the writer's technical knowledge of building maintenance
delay the main claim so the argument arrives as a surprise
prove that the gym was unsafe and had to close
questions.why: Selected concrete detail creates the emotional residue that the abstraction "closure" cannot, which is the point of the description.

questions.stem: A cell secretes a lysosomal enzyme outside the cell instead of delivering it to the lysosome. Which failure best explains this, and at which organelle?
options: A defect in the proteasome, so the enzyme is degraded before it can be sorted
A defect in the Golgi apparatus, so the enzyme is not tagged for lysosomal delivery and follows the default secretory route
A defect in the mitochondrion, so there is not enough ATP for vesicle transport
A defect in the nucleolus, so the enzyme's mRNA is never exported
questions.why: Mannose-6-phosphate tagging in the Golgi sorts hydrolases to lysosomes; without the tag, the default pathway carries them out of the cell.

questions.stem: The same finding on later start times appears in a district memo ("the schedule shift produced a 4 percent attendance gain") and in a parent newsletter ("your kids are showing up rested enough to learn"). The difference is best explained by a change in
options: the underlying evidence, which is stronger in the newsletter
the writer's credibility, which is lower in the memo
the logical structure of the argument, which is reversed in the newsletter
the audience and purpose, which call for different registers and different framing of one finding
questions.why: Rhetorical situation governs diction and framing: an internal audience expects measured administrative prose, parents expect direct second-person stakes.

questions.stem: A recessive X-linked trait appears in a family. Neither parent shows the trait, but half their sons do and none of their daughters do. Which best explains the pattern?
options: The father carries the allele on his X chromosome and passed it to his sons
Both parents are homozygous recessive, so all children inherit two copies
The mother is a heterozygous carrier; sons receive her affected X and express it, while daughters receive a normal X from the father
The trait is autosomal recessive and the sex ratio is a coincidence of small sample size
questions.why: Sons get their only X from the mother, so a carrier mother produces affected sons at 50 percent; daughters with a normal paternal X are unaffected carriers.

questions.stem: "By 'equity' I mean, in this essay, the distribution of lab equipment so that no classroom is more than one station short of need." The writer specifies the term mainly to
options: fix a contested term so the argument can be judged against a stated standard rather than a vague one
show that the writer is uncertain what the word means
concede that the term is meaningless and should be abandoned
introduce a statistic that will be used later as evidence
questions.why: Stipulating a definition removes ambiguity and commits the writer to a standard the reader can hold them to.

questions.stem: A freshwater protozoan placed in distilled water swells but does not burst, and its contractile vacuole beats faster. Which best explains the observation?
options: A cell wall stiffens under hypotonic stress and resists expansion
Water leaves the cell by active transport, so the vacuole only moves ions
The vacuole pumps solutes inward, which draws water back into the cytoplasm
Water enters by osmosis because the cytoplasm is hypertonic to the surroundings, and the vacuole expels the excess
questions.why: Freshwater cytoplasm is hypertonic, so water enters; the contractile vacuole expels it, and a protozoan has no wall to resist swelling.

questions.stem: A student's essay states its claim, presents three supporting studies, then devotes its final paragraph to the strongest objection, ending with "but the evidence above is convincing." The essay's main organizational problem is that it
options: presents too much evidence for a short essay
raises the objection too late and answers it only with assertion, leaving the rebuttal underdeveloped
states its claim too early, which removes suspense
uses published studies instead of personal experience, which weakens credibility
questions.why: A counterargument needs room to be answered; a closing paragraph that merely reasserts the claim concedes ground instead of recovering it.

questions.stem: A DNA sample is cut with a restriction enzyme, run on a gel, and produces two bands, one large and one small. Which statement best explains the migration?
options: The small fragment migrated farther because shorter fragments move more easily through the gel matrix
The large fragment migrated farther because it carries more total charge
Both fragments migrated equally because DNA charge-to-mass ratio is constant; the bands differ only in brightness
The bands reflect single- versus double-stranded DNA rather than fragment length
questions.why: All DNA has the same charge per mass, so separation is by size; the gel mesh retards longer fragments more.

questions.stem: "Across four meetings, two failed votes, and a hundred pages of public comment, the board arrived at a decision no one had proposed in September." Compared with naming the decision first, this sentence mainly
options: confuses the reader by withholding the subject of the sentence
weakens the sentence by adding unnecessary prepositional phrases
builds suspense and emphasizes the effort behind a result that emerged from the process
shifts the sentence from narrative to argumentative purpose
questions.why: Front-loading the process delays the payoff, which is the periodic structure's effect: the reader arrives at the decision the way the board did.

questions.stem: A population of yeast introduced to a fresh flask grows slowly, then rapidly, then levels off as nutrients fall and waste accumulates. Which best describes the curve and its cause?
options: Exponential throughout, because yeast reproduction is not limited by resources
Logistic but with no carrying capacity, because the leveling is an artifact of measurement
Exponential, because the nutrients in the flask are constant and only waste changes
Logistic: growth is exponential while resources are abundant, then slows as density-dependent limits set a carrying capacity
questions.why: The plateau reflects density-dependent limits, nutrient depletion and waste, which is the definition of logistic growth around K.

questions.stem: "The district's plan to 'right-size its facilities' closes two neighborhood schools." A reader who objects to the phrase would most likely argue that it
options: is too technical for a general audience to understand
softens a concrete loss behind administrative language, so the reader must supply what is actually being done
is hyperbole that overstates the size of the schools
is a neutral description that carries no evaluative weight
questions.why: Euphemism replaces a plain description of harm with a managerial abstraction, which blurs responsibility for the decision.

questions.stem: Two genes on the same chromosome produce only parental combinations in 90 percent of offspring and recombinant combinations in 10 percent. Which best explains the 10 percent?
options: The genes assort independently, and the 10 percent is sampling error
The genes lie on separate chromosomes and 10 percent of meiosis is abnormal
Crossing over between the genes during meiosis produces recombinants; the low frequency reflects their close linkage
Mutation creates the recombinant types at a fixed rate per generation
questions.why: Linked genes travel together unless a crossover falls between them; a low recombination frequency indicates they sit close on the chromosome.

questions.stem: "Either the district adopts a year-round calendar or it accepts that students will keep losing ground every summer." The reasoning is flawed because it
options: presents two options as exhaustive when other remedies, such as targeted summer programs, exist
relies on a sample too small to support any conclusion
attacks the character of the people who oppose the calendar
confuses correlation with causation in the summer-learning evidence
questions.why: A false dilemma narrows a larger field of options to two, one of which is made to look unacceptable.

questions.stem: A student tests whether a fertilizer increases plant height: ten treated plants on a sunny windowsill, ten untreated plants in a dark closet. After three weeks the treated plants are taller. The conclusion is invalid mainly because
options: ten plants per group is too few for any statistical test
light and fertilizer vary together, so the height difference cannot be attributed to the fertilizer
plant height is not a measurable dependent variable
the treated plants should have been measured before the untreated ones
questions.why: Two variables differ between the groups, so the design confounds light with fertilizer and supports no causal claim about either.

questions.stem: An essay on a school closure runs a long, clause-heavy sentence describing the last assembly, then: "The building is empty now." The short sentence most likely functions to
options: signal that the writer has run out of relevant detail
break the paragraph's grammar deliberately to seem informal
introduce a new topic the long sentence could not contain
land the emotional weight by contrast, letting brevity carry what the long sentence built
questions.why: The abrupt drop in length after a cumulative sentence isolates the fact and gives it emphasis.

questions.stem: A field abandoned after farming is colonized by grasses and weeds, then shrubs, then a closed canopy of pines, and finally hardwoods. Which best explains the sequence?
options: Each stage alters conditions, soil, light, and moisture, in ways that favor later competitors until a stable community forms
Later species migrate in at a steady rate unrelated to the species already present
The pines suppress the hardwoods permanently, so the sequence stops at pine
The sequence is random and reflects only which seeds happen to arrive first
questions.why: Succession is driven by facilitation and changing conditions: early colonists build soil and shade, shifting the competitive advantage to later species.

questions.stem: "We have waited through three superintendents. We have waited through two bond failures. We have waited through a pandemic." The repetition of "we have waited" mainly
options: shows that the writer has no specific evidence to offer
creates a list of unrelated events to broaden the topic
accumulates grievance and forces the reader to feel the duration, ending on the heaviest instance
softens the tone so the request sounds more reasonable
questions.why: Anaphora builds rhythm and weight through repetition, and the escalation to the pandemic caps the series.

questions.stem: A marathon runner's core temperature rises during a race. Which combination of responses best restores the set point?
options: Vasoconstriction of skin vessels and shivering, which conserve and generate heat
Decreased heart rate and reduced breathing, which lower metabolic heat production
Increased thyroid hormone release and piloerection, which trap a layer of warm air
Vasodilation of skin vessels and sweating, which increase heat loss through radiation and evaporation
questions.why: Cooling is achieved by moving blood to the surface and evaporating sweat; shivering and vasoconstriction are the cold-side responses.

questions.stem: "The district cut the arts budget by 30 percent. ______, math scores rose the following year." Which connective best signals that the writer is refusing to imply that the cut caused the rise?
options: Consequently,
Independently of that decision,
As a result,
Because of the cut,
questions.why: The connective frames the second fact as unconnected, which blocks the causal inference the other three options would invite.

questions.stem: An antibiotic that blocks bacterial ribosomes has no effect on a patient's viral infection. Which best explains why?
options: Viruses are too large for the antibiotic to penetrate
Viruses use host ribosomes, which the antibiotic cannot reach because it does not cross the viral envelope
Viruses lack ribosomes entirely and replicate with host enzymes and machinery, so a bacterial ribosome target does not exist in them
Viruses are killed only by antibiotics that target their cell walls
questions.why: Viruses have no ribosomes or cell wall of their own; they rely on host machinery, so antibacterial targets are simply absent.
